claims.statement: A security valuation is a per-user fair-value range: `SecurityValuationModel` maps to `market_security_valuations` with `user_id` (a plain UUID, no FK to `auth_users`), a cascading `security_id` FK to `market_securities.id`, non-null `lower_bound`/`upper_bound` declared as `DECIMAL(16,8)`, and created/updated timestamps, with `UniqueConstraint("user_id", "security_id", name="valuation_user_security_unique")` plus the index `ix_market_security_valuations_user_security` over the same pair -- so there is at most one range per (user, security).

`migrations/versions/3436586a755f_create_security_valuations.py` (down_revision `4c2ed77e7738`) is the Alembic revision that creates `market_security_valuations` with its cascading foreign key, primary key, the `valuation_user_security_unique` unique constraint and the non-unique `ix_market_security_valuations_user_security` index, and its `downgrade()` drops the index and table, demonstrating the repository rule that a model change ships its revision in the same change under the `<hash>_<description>.py` naming convention.

`SecurityValuationRepository` in `src/market/repository.py` is a router-only ABC with exactly four methods -- `get_by_security_and_user`, `upsert`, `get_batch_by_user_and_securities` and `get_history` -- and its SQLAlchemy implementation filters every statement by `user_id`, so no read or write (including the history read) can cross users.

`SqlAlchemySecurityValuationRepository.upsert` selects the `(security_id, user_id)` row and either overwrites `lower_bound`/`upper_bound` with `updated_at = datetime.now(UTC)` or inserts a new row with both timestamps set to that same `now`; in both branches it then adds a `SecurityValuationHistoryModel` row carrying the same bounds and timestamp, commits once and refreshes -- so the write is idempotent (a second upsert returns the same row `id`, as the repository test asserts) and never updates the current value without appending a revision.

`get_batch_by_user_and_securities` returns `[]` immediately for an empty id list and otherwise issues one `IN` query scoped by `user_id`, so batch reads return only the subset of requested securities that the caller actually has a range for (a second user's row for the same security is excluded, as the repository test asserts).

The market router exposes exactly four valuation routes, all behind `current_user` and all passing `user.id`: `GET /market/securities/{security_id}/valuation` (which raises `HTTPException(404, detail="Valuation not found")` when the repository returns `None`), `PUT /market/securities/{security_id}/valuation` (delegating straight to `upsert` with no security-existence check), and the two batch routes `GET /market/securities/valuation/batch` (repeated `security_ids` query params, `None` coalesced to `[]`) and `POST /market/securities/valuation/batch` (body `SecurityValuationBatchRequest`), which call the same batch repository method.

The valuation payload contract is minimal and there is no server-side ordering rule: `SecurityValuationWrite` carries only `lower_bound` and `upper_bound`, `SecurityValuationRead` echoes `id`, `user_id`, `security_id`, both bounds and both timestamps with `from_attributes=True`, `SecurityValuationHistoryRead` echoes the same minus `updated_at`, and `SecurityValuationBatchRequest` is just `security_ids: list[SecurityId]` -- so `lower_bound <= upper_bound` is enforced only by the frontend modal.

`SecurityValuationRepository` is wired into dependency injection by `sqlalchemy_security_valuation_repository_factory`, registered against the ABC key in `register_market_services` (`src/market/__init__.py`), which is how the router resolves it with `services.aget(SecurityValuationRepository)`.

`ValuationClient.getValuation` is the deliberate exception to the shared `ApiClient` rule that any non-`ok` response throws: it returns `Promise<SecurityValuation | null>` and maps a 404 to `null` through two branches -- an error whose `status` is 404, or an `Error` whose `message` includes `'404'` -- while rethrowing every other error; `saveValuation`/`setValuation` issue the `PUT` with exactly `{ lower_bound, upper_bound }` (silently dropping the interface's optional `notes` field, which the backend schema does not accept), and `getBatchValuations` short-circuits an empty id list to `[]` before POSTing `{ security_ids }`.

`FundamentalsGroup` is the editing surface on the security detail page: it fetches the range via `valuationClient.getValuation(securityId)` inside an untracked `$effect` gated on `expanded && securityId`, renders a skeleton while loading, treats `null` as the "Fair value range not set." empty state (a genuine error instead renders `SidebarError` with a retry bound to `fetchValuation`), and otherwise shows both bounds currency-formatted with an en dash, an Edit affordance, the "Show on chart" checkbox and the `valuation-updated-at` date; it passes the range into `ValuationModal` whose `onSaved` writes the returned row straight back into the two-way-bound `valuation` (and thus the chart) without a refetch.

`ValuationModal` is the only validation point for a range: on submit it re-rounds both inputs with `Math.round(Number(v) * 100) / 100` and then rejects a null or non-positive lower bound, a null or non-positive upper bound, and a `lowerBound > upperBound` pair with an inline message before calling `valuationClient.setValuation`, and on success invokes `onSaved`, closes the modal and leaves a thrown error as the banner text -- so the client is never called with an inverted range.

Whether the band is drawn is a separate preference from whether a range is stored: the security page seeds `showValuationOverlay` from `prefs.show_valuation_band` in `onPreferencesLoaded` and in its init-chain preferences fetch (each guarded by an explicit undefined/null check), the fundamentals group's "Show on chart" checkbox persists it with `userPreferencesService.patchPreferences({ show_valuation_band: val })` and only logs a failure, and the page forwards the same flag into the chart as both `showValuation` and `showValuationBand`.

Before rendering, the band is gated inside the chart by `isValuationBandVisible = showValuationBand !== undefined ? showValuationBand : showValuation`, so the narrower `showValuationBand` prop wins; the primitive is constructed from the range only when that flag is true and one `$effect` pushes updates through `setRange(visible ? lower_bound : null, visible ? upper_bound : null, visible)`, meaning hiding the band passes `null` bounds rather than detaching the primitive.

`ValuationBandPrimitive` renders the range as a single bottom-z-ordered pane on the main series: `ValuationBandPaneView.zOrder()` returns `'bottom'`, and `ValuationBandRenderer.draw` returns without drawing when `visible` is false, either bound is null, or no series is attached, otherwise converting both prices with `series.priceToCoordinate()` and filling the rectangle between them with a translucent blue plus dashed stroke lines at each bound inside `useBitmapCoordinateSpace`.

Two non-chart surfaces read ranges in bulk through `MarketService.getValuationsBatch` (the POST batch route) rather than `ValuationClient`: `HoldingsService.load` collects the distinct `security_id`s from loaded rows, coerces the raw `number | string` bounds with `Number(...)` into a `{ [security_id]: SecurityValuation }` map inside a nested try/catch that degrades to `{}` so a valuation failure never fails the holdings load, and the `/watchlists` page fetches the same batch in a cancellable `$effect` for its Valuation column.

Range display falls back to an em dash rather than a fabricated value: `formatValuationRange` in `$lib/utils/finance/valuation.ts` formats both bounds to two decimals with an `en-CA` formatter and an en-dash separator and returns `—` when either bound is missing or non-finite, while `formatValuationRange` in `watchlist-utils.ts` takes the valuation object and also returns `—` when absent or blank; the holdings table additionally sorts the Valuation Range column by the midpoint of the two bounds, with null cells sorted last.

The valuation feature's focused tests sit at four layers: `tests/market/test_security_valuation_repository.py` (not-found returns `None`, upsert create/update preserving the row id, batch isolation between users, empty list returns `[]`) against the ephemeral Postgres session, `tests/routers/test_market.py` for the 404-before-write plus PUT/GET round trip and both batch forms, `frontend/src/lib/api/valuationClient.test.ts` for the 404-to-null mapping and PUT body, and the component/chart suites (`fundamentals-group.test.ts`, `valuation-modal.test.ts`, `valuation-band.test.ts`, `security-chart.test.ts`) which mock the API clients and `lightweight-charts`.

`SecurityValuationHistoryModel` maps to `market_security_valuation_history` with the same `user_id`, cascading `security_id` FK and two `DECIMAL(16, 8)` bounds but only a single `created_at` and no unique constraint (one row per write), indexed by `ix_market_security_valuation_history_user_security_created` over `(user_id, security_id, created_at)`; it was added in the later revision `migrations/versions/b291707f24ca_add_market_security_valuation_history.py` (`down_revision = "7e9699e1590e"`), whose `downgrade()` drops the index and table.

`get_history(security_id, user_id)` returns every revision row for that pair ordered by `created_at` then `id` ascending as `SecurityValuationHistoryRead`, and it has no HTTP surface: the router exposes only the four current-value routes and no frontend client references history, so the append-only log is reachable only from code that resolves `SecurityValuationRepository` itself (the repository test pins empty-before-write, two ordered revisions after two upserts, and isolation from other users' and securities' rows).

The chart's valuation prop is rewind-aware: the security page passes `drawingsService.effectiveValuation`, which returns the live `valuation` when not rewound and `activeSnapshot.drawings.valuation` (or `null` when that snapshot carries no range) when rewound; saving a range calls `handleValuationSave`, which sets the live valuation and then awaits `handleSaveSnapshot()`, persisting a snapshot whose `drawings.valuation` holds `Number(...)`-coerced bounds and where a valuation alone counts as content so the save still happens with no drawings at all.

Two frontend clients read the same valuation payload with deliberately different bound types: `ValuationClient` declares numeric `lower_bound`/`upper_bound` (and aliases `SecurityValuationRead` to it) for the detail page and fundamentals group, while `MarketService` declares `SecurityValuationRead` with `number | string` bounds plus a separate numeric `SecurityValuation` for table rows -- so coercion lives in the consumers, with `HoldingsService.load` normalizing each batch entry via `Number(...)` while the `/watchlists` page keeps the raw objects and coerces inside `formatPrice`.

`ValuationModal` rounds before it validates: it prefills and re-rounds both bounds with `Math.round(Number(v) * 100) / 100` (inputs are `type="number"` with `step="0.01"` and `min="0"`), so a sub-cent entry such as `0.004` becomes `0` and is rejected as non-positive, and stored values such as `100.456`/`150.789` are displayed as `100.46`/`150.79`.
